utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that there was some procedural issues to be raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Once again, I have to regretfully notify the Chamber that we received another six exhibits last night from the Office of the Prosecutor that were not on the exhibit list. Photographs of Obrovac, a map of Obrovac, a map of Gracac city, a map of Benkovac. Certainly nothing that happened during the course of Mr. Rajcic's testimony yesterday elicited the need to go back to the archives of the Office of the Prosecutor to put these documents on the witness list [sic] and not on the 65 ter list. Well, if can I look at them. One of them is -- the 4866 is on it and 6165 is part of P549, but the others are not. In any event, none of them were on the exhibit list, and at this juncture, Mr. President, this has been going on for weeks, my question rhetorically is when does it end? There has been a continuous flouting of the rules by the Prosecution to the extent that the Prosecution believes that there are no rules concerning disclosure. And that's in fact we are at this juncture. I bring it to Your Honours' attention again. I certainly can read the 65 ter numbers that were sent to us late last night, not late last night, but last evening. And we can object to this practice. We object to all of these exhibits coming into evidence and the late disclosure, and it continues to be something that prejudices the Defence and continues to be something that the Prosecution fails to justify and show good cause to the Chamber, why they continue to conduct themselves in this fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The exhibits that were sent over as Mr. Kehoe indicated, the maps of Benkovac, Gracac, and Obrovac are all on the 65 ter list. One of them is in fact an enlargement of an admitted exhibit. In any event, these are unmarked maps. We have any number of maps of Sector South which, if enlarged would simply show the same thing I'm going to be showing to the witness and asking him to identify the locations of targets. I don't understand what the prejudice is of showing the witness an unmarked map that I'm not going to be admitting. I'm going to be seeking to admit what he puts on the map, which obviously I could not have provide notice of. I'm not sure what the argument is that there's a problem with using a map as a demonstrative aid to testimony, in any case, as I indicated, although they were clearly not on the first exhibit list or the amended exhibit list that I sent over, they are on the 65 ter list and even in evidence. To suggest that there is some form of prejudice by putting in an unmarked map of something that is part of many admitted exhibits doesn't seem to make sense. In any event, Your Honour, on cross-examination the Prosecution often receives additional documents from the Defence during the course of cross-examination. We don't make an issue of that. It does happen that sometimes what witnesses say may bring another document to the mind of the examiner. I don't see where that's a problem. The witness indicated yesterday that he personally planned the targets for Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac. That was not indicated in any of the documents that we have. I was going ask him what the targets were to the extent he could recall. But now that he indicates that he planned it out, it seems it would make sense to ask him to indicate to the Court the locations of those targets. That's all I have to say, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will deal with the matter on a case-by-case basis. Of course, when the matter was raised, the Chamber was unaware of whether these were unmarked maps. Once we see the exhibits, we'll see whether there's anything more than just a map, and we'll then see to what extent it is prejudicial to use that exhibit. That's the way in which we will proceed. There is anything else to be raised at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, on that score, I don't know if we're going to get to these maps, but certainly 65 ter 7169, that is apparently taken from P190, or records reflect have not yet even been disclosed in e-court, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it will be used, then we can have a look at it, and -- Mr. Russo, I do understand and there's no misunderstanding that it is just blank maps as -- just as to be used as an aid rather as the maps in itself having any probative value.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is not completely accurate. There are photographs as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I meant maps and photographs. I was not very precise in that. Any other ... Then the Chamber has one question for you, Mr. Mikulicic. You asked to be present at the other side of the line in a videolink testimony. The Chamber would like to hear from you what the specific reasons why you want to be there rather than here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only specific reason which I had in mind is that is completely different situation when the Defence is dealing with a very important witness in situ than via the videolink. So my attention was when I ask for it, to be present in situ so that I can be close to witness to see his reaction on my question, to see the conversation and the cross-examination between the Defence counsel and the witness in every -- in every way is much more personal when the both of them are in the very same room, in the courtroom. So my intention was to be in situ as to provide the best possible cross-examination on behalf of my client. And when I check the rules I see no reason what that couldn't be allowed. So that was my request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me then first ask, Mr. Russo, the wish to be present at the other side of the videolink, or in situ as Mr. Mikulicic tells us, would that still exist if the Defence would not be there? Is it totally dependant on the meeting the -- the wishes of the Defence? Or is there any independent reason why the Prosecution would like to be at the other end of the line?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, are you asking me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'm saying, you said if Mr. Mikulicic will be there, then someone of the Prosecution should be there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Saklaine said that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that. But if for whatever reason Mr. Mikulicic would not be there, would there still be a wish to be present at the other end of the line?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it is totally dependant ... The Chamber will have to balance the advantages which you just explained and the disadvantages that may be there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would just like to stress one point, although I think I did it already. This is a very, very important witness for the Markac Defence. So it is my opinion that I, by all means, have to be present in the very same room with that witness to conduct a proper cross-examination, and that is also a wish and a request of my client as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that you do this upon instructions. You say it's a very important witness. I'd like to see how the witness response. Is there anything else, anything specific? Why is it -- why is this witness so important for that you that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Maybe just to add, Your Honour, on that topic, I should use a lot of documents in cross-examination of that witness, so the manipulation of the documents is obviously much more convenient in situ situation than via the videolink, although that is that very much depends on the technical facilities. But any way, I do really strongly request that I have to be present in situ in Zagreb office while the cross-examination should be conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has in the Prosecution any specific view on the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I believe there is an concern, especially given the fact there will be a protective measures motion for the witness that there is a concern that if the witness sees simply accused for one -- counsel for one accused of whom he will be offering testimony, it may tend to make him think that this is, for some reason, which he is unable to discern, it may cause the witness additional hesitation in offering testimony. I'm not sure what the specific advantages are that Mr. Mikulicic points out. I understand it may be to his preference to be in the room, look the witness in the eye, observe the witness's demeanour on testimony. However, that, I would submit, is for the finder of fact to evaluate the demeanor of the witness, not for counsel. It's for that reason, Your Honour, not sure having a videolink with individuals present during the questioning is necessary. But that is why we would also seek to be present, if Mr. Mikulicic is permitted to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course, I have nothing to object at the request of the -- my learned friend from the Prosecution office. That is obviously. And I don't think that the reasoning as to the witness could be in a way intimidated by the presence of only one counsel. I think this is not a reason for this at all. Why should the witness feel himself uncomfortable because only one counsel is present in situ I cannot see reason for it. Anyway, why should the witness be uncomfortable at all? I mean, on the other side it is a Prosecution witness, and the Prosecution could instruct the witness on procedural matters in that case, in that very specific case, so I can see no reason why not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Mr. Mikulicic, how do you imagine this to be done? Usually in a videolink the Chamber has a constant view on the witness. How did you imagine that the camera would be used at the other side of the line, if there would be two counsel and one witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously, I'm not very good in technicalities, so I haven't those circumstances in my mind when asking for it. The only -- the only preference was that I simply should comply my client's request and cross-examination on the very best way that I can do. So I haven't in mind those technicalities, but I mean, just talking at the top of my head, that could be placed two cameras, so one camera could be focussed on examiner, whether it will be a Prosecution colleague on the place, or will be I, or myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and would we then receive all the imagines simultaneously in your mind or ... because it is more than just technicalities. I take it that you understand that it's more than just the voltage and the zoom in or out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am aware of your concern, but what is my position, is that the right of accused vice versa the technical possibilities is something that could not be compared. So whatever it is, I think the right of accused is to be prevailed in such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the right of the accused being what exactly? You're referring to what right exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm exactly aiming at the right of accused to have an undisturbed cross-examination via witness who is, in that case, particularly very important for the Defence. So I think it is quite obvious that there is completely different situation to examine the witness via videolink than to examine the witness sitting in a very same room with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we're not mistaken -- I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic was first on his feet, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would just going to add that there, of course, is a -- in response to Mr. Russo, there is a legitimate forensic purpose in cross-examination to being able to confront a witness in person versus via videolink, which is I think what my colleague Mr. Mikulicic is trying to emphasise. And I just wanted to recall that I think we've had one experience before, the Chamber will recall, with a witness who in middle of cross-examination was willing to even set up a videolink so he wouldn't have to come back at that point, and that's precisely where we're getting at in terms of -- I think the Chamber then made special arrangements to make sure that that witness could come back specifically for that forensic purpose in cross-examination. I understand that the Chamber has had to weigh the technical possibilities versus that forensic advantage. But I did want to put that on the record, in response to Mr. Russo. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry. If I'm not mistaken, I think there was at least one occasion when the Prosecution was present at a videolink conducting direct examination of a protected witness, and I'm almost sure that it happened on one occasion, and it was a -- I can't remember if was a woman protected witness or a male protected witness, but I do recall one occasion that that occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think this should be a gender-neutral issue. Apart from that, Mr. Russo, I have to -- was this in this case? I may have ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't recall that happening. But I assume if it happened, it is easily found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will have a look at it at least, and also we'll then consider whether there were any specific reasons, and the Chamber will further consider your request, Mr. Mikulicic. Could I ask whether the other Defence teams would also then want to be present for cross-examination purposes? Or slowly we move to a situation where almost the Bench could go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: We would not seek to be present, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Nor would we, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to add something. Is my understanding that the kind of procedures that we're dealing with on the everyday basis is a procedure that is prescripted by the rules as a so-called normal circumstances. The videolink is kind of exceptional circumstances where, according to 81 bis, Chamber may order in the interest of justice. So if we have this in mind, and when we are arguing whether I could be present or not, I think that is something that I would like the Chamber as to concerned of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll consider all the submissions made by the parties, and the Chamber will give a ruling soon. Now, what was the date scheduled, do we remember, Mr. Mikulicic? So that we -- I take it that if you want to be present, you have to prepare to make arrangements, so, therefore, it is in your interest to know as soon as possible -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that will be -- that wouldn't be a problem for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But for when was it -- was the testimony scheduled exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe it's the 26th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 26th of February. Today it's the 19th. That would be -- yes, 26th or 27th. The Chamber will further consider the matter, and to the extent possible, already inform you about the outcome of our deliberations on this matter before the weekend, Mr. Mikulicic. If not, we'll certainly be in touch with you through our legal officer to tell you when you can expect a decision, but we're trying to have it done before the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one other procedural matter. The Court will recall when Witness Lausic testified that there was a discussion, and he was asked to provide his original diary to the Zagreb office of the ICTY. I just wanted to note that we still have not received anything, and I wanted to get that before the end of the Prosecution's case, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The registry informs me that the material will arrive in The Hague either late this week or early next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Russo, are you ready to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. I just wanted to advise everyone that the first exhibit I'm going to be showing the witness is the map of Benkovac, and I'm going to show him the other maps, just so that everybody is clear that is what I am going to be doing in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you can have -- already look at the map to see what the map is and -- but it's just a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Sure. That's 65 ter 5186.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps waiting for the arrival of the witness, perhaps we could already have a look at it. Mr. Kehoe, if this map would be used, you oppose against admissions because it was not on the exhibit list. Could you further explain what the prejudice would be if this map was used to -- to indicate locations, because that's what I expect Mr. Russo to ask the witness to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It has to do with -- yes, Mr. President, it has to do with pre-trial preparation. Naturally, Your Honour, you were trial counsel, when you get exhibits from the other side, you go back, look at those exhibits, examine your files, and do pre-trial preparation with those exhibits. During the course of our -- the rolling disclosure by the Prosecution having had this map, certainly we would have taken extensive time to go through all the information knowing that the Prosecution was going to used it. We didn't know they were going to use it until late last night.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I prefer to have the witness out of the courtroom while the basis for Mr. Kehoe's objection is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one second only. Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So frankly, Your Honour, it would go to pre-trial preparation. Certainly as we informed Your Honour, we were discussing a variety of matters with Mr. Rajcic during last week, and during this role in discovery, we certainly showed him many of the exhibits that were part of his annex that were coming in that the Prosecution intended to tender. And certainly this would have been one we would have shown him as well. So even putting that aside just for our own purposes internally, know what the Prosecution is going to attempt to offer goes directly to our pre-trial preparation, which, again, because of the Prosecutor's conduct, they have prevented us from doing so. Or to the extent that we have been able to do it, we have to do it at the last minute and -- this is just gone on and on, and this is just another instance of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, just to put matters straight, I take it your objection is against the use of this map and not about asking questions to the witness about targets he may have identified or determined in the Benkovac -- town of Benkovac or the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we take this -- if we take this particular map parenthetically and just look at this map, yes, that's the case. But again, in response to what Mr. Russo said previously, these are a series of violations which I think [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kehoe. I asked you a specific question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not invite you to repeat what you said earlier as the basis of your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked whether there is any objection against Mr. Russo asking questions about targets in Benkovac in -- or around Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I believe my answer to that is, no. He can certainly ask that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, yes. Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the basis of what has been said until now, the Chamber sees no reason to sustain the objection. We'll finally decide the matter at the -- once the map is tendered. Good morning, Mr. Rajcic. Mr. Rajcic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony, that you would speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Russo will now continue his examination-in-chief. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You see before you on the screen a map of the area of Benkovac. I'd like to you please indicate, if I could have the assistance of the court usher, I'm going to ask to you indicate the areas where the targets that were fired upon by Croatian forces were located, and I would like to take them one by one. Now, first if you could tell us if you need this image enlarged any, you can let us know.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, thanks, this will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: As I said, I would like to take the targets one by one. So if you could first tell us in order of importance; that is in order of military significant, what the first target was in Benkovac that you fired at.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first target at Benkovac was the Slobodan Macura barracks; the second was the police station; the third target was the cross-roads and a barracks right above the toponym Benkovacko Selo, but I don't think I can see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if you would, please, circle the Slobodan Macura barracks. And if you are unable to circle only that barracks, then we can have the image enlarged so that you circle only what you fired at. So just let us know if you need us to enlarge it, if not, please circle that barracks and place a number 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have the right colour for marking? I always forget which --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It's been a while, Your Honour. I think we are red.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're red. You can mark that on the screen. Madam Usher, perhaps you assist the witness. Please mark the first targets, if you take it one by one, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Please circle the Slobodan Macura barracks and place a number 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Slobodan Macura barracks is in the direction of Klicevica, hereabouts. The police station was precisely determined by the X and Y coordinates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you add a 1 next to the barracks, and a 2 to the police station.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe you indicated that the third target was the cross-roads. Can you please circle which cross-roads you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I would have to look it up on the map. I'll put a number 3 next to it. And the fourth high-payoff target was in this direction, above this toponym, but we can't see it, we should have to scroll up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you simply place the number 4 directly above the word Benkovacko.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 4. But this isn't accurate because the target was further to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that. Thank you. We'll note that for the record. Were there any other targets inside the town of Benkovac that were fired at by Croatian forces on either the 4th or 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information or reports from Artillery Group 5 to be able to say within a degree of certainty whether they fired at that target. Relying on my memory, without a table of targets or the map that we looked at yesterday, and which was used in the book, I would have to look up the numbers assigned to these targets and possible other targets in the periphery of Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And the map that you're referring to, which map is that that you would need to look at?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Russo, yesterday we spoke about the map showing the plan of activity of the artillery which was made for the book, and the book says for Artillery Group 5 -- or mentions several marks, and I believe that these marks are 301 and further -- it continues in sequence. That's the map I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And just to be clear, is that the map which contained the rectangular target boxes?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The map which was graphically edited and on which Mr. Brkljaca wrote. There are numerical marks of the areas where the targets were located, and next to each rectangle there was a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you recall from the version of the map which we showed you yesterday, which was simply an enlargement of the picture that appears in the book, do you know where either the original or a copy of that map is?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us when the last time you saw a copy of that map was and where?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I should have been a little bit more clear. Not a copy in the book itself or what I showed you yesterday. The actual -- you indicated that the original map was copied for the book. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Russo, that is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell me then, if you know, where the original of that map is?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Other than the copy that's in the book, do you know where any other copies of that map are?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Russo. You're talking about copies. There is no copy of the original. In Croatian, the -- every detail from the original was transmitted or copied by hand upon another -- another copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And that other copy that you're talking about, do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, again, fail to understand "the other copy." If you mean the copy which was hand-drawn, drawn by hand, that was used for scanning and compressing it to A4 format, so that it can be used as an attachment to the book, if that's what you're referring to. I think it should have been made, and this documentation which was manually made, rather than copied mechanically or by means of -- or using technological aids was in the possession of General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how do you know it was in the possession of General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once we finished manually copying these maps, the procedure was the following. The next step was scanning and putting on photographic film. This was used for printing the book. All these sets were bound in files and placed with General Gotovina. I know because the second edition of the book, when it was being published, all that material was again -- and I repeat, it was manually copied, was used for the second edition of the book, because there were two editions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw that manual copy in General Gotovina's possession?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I have a problem with ... I was still working as a chief of department at the main defence inspectorate. When the second edition of the book was being prepared, one map was missing from the set; I don't remember which. I don't remember -- or, rather, sorry. It was necessary to make a new manual copy. As far as I remember, General Gotovina was still the chief inspector. Based on the book, I, once more, copied this miniature version of the map, of -- A4 format copied to another map, and that was then again scanned and compressed and put on film. That's the last time I saw that map, which was used for the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to continue asking you a few questions about this particular map. However, first I'd like to finish with the map we have on the screen right now of Benkovac, so we'll come back to the map that you saw in General Gotovina's possession. With respect to what's in -- what you circled here in Benkovac, did you plan to fire at any other targets than the ones you've indicated on this map?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, in the wider area around Benkovac, the focus of our planned fire and our marking of enemy positions was in the area of Kozlovac. There is the north western part, above the topographic mark Skupac. It is marked as a well, because that is the usual way wells are marked on a map. And there is a road in yellow --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Sorry. I don't mean to cut you off. I should have been more specific with my question. I'm only seeking targets inside the town of Benkovac proper. Other that the ones that you have circled here, numbers 1, 2, and 3, were there any other targets inside Benkovac proper that you had planned to fire artillery at?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I cannot remember now. The premium targets I remember. There may have been more, possibly along the roads leading out from the city, toward the periphery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did anyone -- or were any of the artillery units of the Croatian forces firing at targets in Benkovac that you did not select?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information that they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If, in fact, they had, as the chief of artillery for the Split Military District, would that information have come to your attention?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the standard operating procedure, they would have had to inform me of such incidents from the forward command post in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would offer the exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Mr. Registrar, would you please assign an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit P2327.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Map marked by the witness and is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go into private session for just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you recognise this map as the one that we looked at yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We also looked at this map yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And, first, can you confirm whether this is a precise copy of its original?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, again, when was the last time that you saw the original of this map?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were working on the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is that the first edition of the book?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first edition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I think the purpose to get it on the screen was to identify whether this was the map shown and left in the hands of the Gotovina Defence or whether it was another map. I do understand that this is not the map. Could you please seek confirmation of that. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, first, if we could go into private session for one minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, did you give a copy of this map to the Gotovina Defence?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And do you know where any accurate-sized copies of this map; in other words, ones in which we can see inside the target boxes where you indicated that it would be numbers. Do you know where any copies of that are?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A copy of the map we have on our screens now is something that I don't know the whereabouts of. Save for the fact that I see it here and that I have a signed book, I don't know where the map can be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could now have Exhibit P2322, MFI. And if we could move to page 3 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at this map on the screen, Mr. Rajcic, do you recognise this as the map that we took a look at -- one of the maps that we took a look at yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the map, a copy of my original, that we looked at yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And is this the map that you gave to the Gotovina Defence for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could now have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, yesterday the witness testified that he made a mistake when drafting this map. And it was unclear to me what the effect of the mistake would have been, in terms of understanding the reach of the weaponry, and I'd like you to explore that, perhaps to ask him what exactly is wrong. He said to some extent it was not on this map. Of course, now we have cut out part of it. If I look at the -- page 3 in its entirety, perhaps we can show it to the witness and ask him to indicate where the mistake is because I have got no idea whether it has any consequence for any followup matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. My understanding was, and I think Counsel will correct me if I'm wrong, that the mistake was with respect to the sector of fire for a 203-millimetre weapon, that it was not accurately depicted on this map. It is my understanding from the witness's testimony that was not one of the weapons that fired on Knin. Nevertheless, I will explore with the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the parties agree that it's a matter which has no further consequences, then, of course, I'm satisfied with that. But not knowing it, I want to -- wanted to explore whether two weeks from now, five weeks from now, we have question which is not answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe my learned friend's assessment is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we don't have to pay any further attention to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could please have 65 ter 7169. And this is a map of Obrovac. If we could just focus a bit more on the area of Obrovac proper. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, I'd like to engage in the same exercise here with Obrovac as we did for Benkovac and have you identify for us the targets that were actually fired at on the 4th and 5th of August by the Croatian forces. And again let's take them one by one, beginning with the most high-value target.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which targets were fired at in Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Who planned the targets in Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was planning them for Obrovac, when it comes to the artillery rocket groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And are you simply unable to recall what those targets were?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the artillery of the corps, I think that one of the plans included only the bridge in Benkovac [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness apparently marked the bridge. Could I invite you to put a letter -- a 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think he is talking about Obrovac. Is -- the translation on 34:15 says Benkovac, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have the map of Obrovac in front of us. Therefore, I take it that must be a mistake. You did mark the bridge in Obrovac as -- as a target you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the level of planning, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So not to say that it was fired at, but that was a planned target.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you indicate to us any other planned targets in Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town of Obrovac itself, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And I notice that your answer was -- your first indication of a target was specifically with respect to corps artillery. Were there any targets which were planned to be fired at by artillery units other than the corps artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For engaging the targets by subordinate units, the chiefs of artillery were the ones drafting the use of artillery plans in the brigades, based on the intelligence they received.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Were the targets that were selected by the chiefs of artillery in Obrovac, were they sent to either you or to General Gotovina for review or approval?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the procedure in place; in other words, that General Gotovina should receive such a report. I have the documents at my disposal, and I coordinate my work with chiefs of artillery of the various units, and that's how we complete the planning stage. Preparations, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That was my question. I wanted to know if either you or General Gotovina were made aware of what targets were selected by the operational group chiefs of artillery. Were you made aware of those?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of the targets selected or fired at, for that matter, in Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know if General Gotovina was aware of what targets were fired at in Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, if you don't know what targets were fired at by the operations group chiefs of artillery, how do you know they complied with the order given to shell the town of Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the chain of command, the first filter is the brigade commander, in accordance with strict instructions. The second filter is the commander of the operations group. And then we come to the level of the Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that. What I'm attempting to determine is how you know whether -- if you don't know what they fired at, then how do you know if they're doing what they were told to do or doing something else?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I base my statement on the fact that it was a disciplined army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, could we further explore the witness exactly meant when he said, page 35, line 18: "I have the documents at my disposal, and I coordinate my work with chiefs of artillery." Witness, what documents were you referring to, and what kind of coordination you meant there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was the procedure: I was referring to the database of all the targets selected, based on the information gathering concerning the lie of the land and the general area. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. So once such a database is produced for the entire area, every intelligence officer of the brigade works out, together with his chief of artillery, the possible firing positions within their area of responsibility. In this way, a precise selection is made and firing tables or documents produced for the detected positions or targets. That's the sort of the documentation I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe we should check page 37, line 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the last three words, I believe the reference was to a different document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said: "In this way, a precise selection is made," and you said then what was produced. You said something that was produced for the detected positions or targets. What was produced? It's -- Mr. Misetic thinks it might be mistranslated, so if you would please repeat that portion of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to the drafting of a final document, containing a list of targets for every area of responsibility of the unit facing the enemy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No firing tables were prepared at that stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. So you have a full set now of a -- as you said, a -- a database with targets, and then targets would be selected at the brigade level. Were you then informed about what targets had been selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had information from the chief of artillery, or chiefs of artillery, of the brigades, and I saw that sort of document containing a selection of targets up to the level of the possible engagement of brigade artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think then what Mr. Russo tried to learn is whether there were any such targets in - we're talking about Obrovac - that you were aware of, you learned about through this selection procedure and follow-up information to you. Any other target than the one you indicated on the map, which was the bridge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. I haven't seen this in 15 years, so I can only rely on my memory. In principle, in planning, you mark the targets, if I can mark it here, along the communications lines leading out of Benkovac [as interpreted], and I remember this cross-roads here. But I repeat, I'm now speaking from memory. I cannot assert this with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you at least put a 2 next to the circle you just marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 38, line 17, again, Benkovac is mentioned and not Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President did you intend --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's -- You refer to this cross-roads near to Obrovac? On our transcript, it appears as Benkovac, but that's apparently a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot influence that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. He circled several things and a 2 next to one. Are we talking about 2 for all of those, for the Chamber's purposes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I missed one, as a matter of fact. You circled the bridge. You added a 1 to that. There was a cross-roads south of Obrovac where you did put a 2. Now you also circled something which appears in red as quite close to the river, a little bit west from the centre of Obrovac, where we see in red 6A. Could you tell us what was that, not a cross-roads, but a road leading out of Obrovac? Is that why you marked it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's a road leading out of Obrovac, westward and along the river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the eastern -- the eastern road runs along the river too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you have marked that. So what you did, you marked the exit road north of the river, eastbound and westbound, and a cross-roads just south of Obrovac as the targets that are still in your memory, targets brigade level. Now you add immediately another marking, which is also an exit road south of the town of Obrovac, where the road seems to be a hairpin. It's now marked five times. I think we can stop marking at this moment, Mr. Rajcic, and if we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. It was all in good intentions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have visualized that exit roads that were in your memory as a planned targets. Mr. Russo, if you tender it very quickly into evidence, then you avoid further marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Mr. President, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, of course, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The witness indicated at page 38, line 14, he says: "I'm not sure. I haven't seen this in 15 years, so I can only rely on my memory. In principle, in planning you mark the targets. If can I mark it here." And then he indicates these -- I was under the impression that the witness was marking what he thought, in principle, would be selected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood this to be what he would expect to be and what is not contradicted by his memory. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: On that basis, Your Honour, I will offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Same objection, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the objection is denied. Mr. Registrar, would you please assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit P2328.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2328, map of Obrovac marked by the witness, is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I realize it is time for a break. I would just ask for one thing over the break. The witness has now been provided with copies of his documents. In particular, I'd like to ask the Court ask him to review the Official Note without discussing it further, so we can get from him what it is in there he either agrees with or disagrees with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The suggestion is that we give some homework to the witness. I hear of no objections.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No break?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... once again, and if the witness could take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your headphones off for a second, Mr. Rajcic. Yes, he has to stay here because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what counsel has gotten in mind, if there was some type of adoption procedure in mind. But, again, this was a document that was made for the purposes of this proceeding. It is it not his statement, and in no fashion should it be this -- this methodology be a use for him to adopt the statement, certainly when going through an exercise of asking questions, if that is it where counsel is going, we object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not going to reargue the issue about the Official Notes. This is an Official Note. You know our position about which proceeding it was taken for. It purports to be a summary of the witness's statement. I don't think there is a problem with asking the witness to look at it and to agree or disagree with whatever portions are in there that he may have said or not said, during his interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic. Mr. Rajcic, you will be provided with an Official Note in your own language -- well, I don't have to explain to you, I take it, what an Official Note purports to be. That is, that's a summary of a statement. Now, what the Chamber would like you to do and what Mr. Russo invited us to ask you, is that you read through it during the next break - we will not deprive you from your coffee but some of your time - and then identify portions where you disagree. That means that you deny that this reflects what you said during that interview and other portions where you said, Well, this reflects what I said, even though not in your own precise words, but the gist of what you said is reflected accurately in the Official Note. Would you be willing to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm willing to do that. Coffee is good, and that will make up for everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break, and we will resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, thank you for giving up some of your time. Mr. Russo, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, briefly two matters. First of all, in view of the timing, the Chamber will explore possibilities to find additional time in court so as not to -- and will, as always, consult with the parties and look in everyone's agenda to see whether we can find some additional time in court. Second, Mr. Kuzmanovic, you, I think it was you who drew our attention to videolink with counsel present at the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I looked at that, and I'm probably mistaken. I -- it was -- registry I was thinking of and not -- I looked, myself, at all the transcripts for the protected witnesses, and I was going to let the Court know that before the end of the day. I was wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are always a bit hesitant, and so if we do not know something that it isn't there because it could well be, but it seems that our findings are concurrent in this respect. Mr. Russo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could please have 65 ter 4866. Mr. President, I don't know if we're still in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I should have put this on the record. We ended last -- the last portion of the hearing, we ended in private session, and upon on my instruction, Mr. Registrar made the start of this -- part of the session in open session, as you can see on the transcript. It was done upon my instructions and, therefore, the approval is there. But it's good that the parties know where we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. 65 ter 4866. And if we could enlarge the section of the town of Gracac proper. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I'm going to ask you to engage in the same exercise here and ask to you please identify, if you can, the targets which, to your knowledge were actually fired at by Croatian forces on the 4th and 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the same exercise? Actually fired at, was the exercise on the previous maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It was the exercise in terms of Benkovac. In terms of Obrovac, I believe the witness indicated to us he didn't recall which ones were actually fired at, and then we defaulted to the planning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I take issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not my recollection as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Not mine either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear that you're now asking this for Gracac. But it's not my recollection that the same question was put, and if I am wrong, Mr. Russo, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I will have a look at that, Your Honour. In that case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will also have a look at it, and to the extent I can assist you, I will do so. But it's clear now that for Gracac, you're asking to indicate targets that were fired at ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In Operation Storm. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, if you would not mind please indicating to us first the target of highest value that was fired upon by Croatian forces in Gracac on the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't show it you here, because this was the operations axis of the special MUP unit under the command of General Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Are you unaware of anything that was fired at in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not aware of the targets fired at in Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did the artillery group TS-5 fire at any targets in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You drew the plans for artillery for the corps artillery; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made the plan of use, but I did not have an overseeing role in its execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did your plan include TS-5 firing on any targets in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell us why you don't know whether that plan was executed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I received an order from General Gotovina on the 3rd of August at 9.45 in Zadar, in the presence of General Markac, his Chief of Staff, I believe, and chief of artillery. General Gotovina issued the order to me -- issued the order to me verbally and told me that I should detach elements of artillery from Artillery Group 5 for operational purposes of the forces of the MUP special unit under the command of General Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that the order to be -- that you detach certain elements of Artillery Group 5 for operational purposes of the MUP, did that leave TS-5 with no artillery? Or did TS-5, after that detachment, still have artillery which it could use, according to your plan?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was left without that part of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And with the artillery that was left to it, the artillery which remained with TS-5, is there a reason why that artillery did not carry out your plan to fire on targets in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was that Gracac was not within their range, as well as Benkovac -- or, rather, sorry, Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, I just want to be clear about what you're telling us before I ask you to mark anything on the map. You -- you are not aware of anything that was fired at in Gracac by either the corps artillery, brigade artillery, or MUP special police units; is that correct? You do don't have any idea what anybody fired at in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, you don't agree with what I'm saying; or, no, you are not aware of any of that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, prepares we try to clarify the earlier issue that ... In relation to Benkovac you asked, What were the targets fired at? The witness marked them on the map. Then you asked him whether any other targets were fired at, to his knowledge. Then we moved to Obrovac. There you started putting the same question to you. When the witness said he didn't know, then we continued with targets, not necessarily fired upon, but then he pointed to the bridge and to the exit roads, et cetera. So the second exercise developed in a bit different way as the first exercise developed. And I think for Gracac everything now is clear from the answers. Does this sufficiently clarify the issue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Given, Mr. Rajcic, that you can't give us any information about what was actually fired at, I would like to discuss the plans which you had drawn, the targets which you had selected in Gracac to be fired at. Could you please indicate to us those targets, only inside the town of Gracac proper, that you had planned for TS-5 to fire artillery at?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will not be 100 percent precise. Generally speaking, the following were planned. Cross-roads, for 130-millimetre cannons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you mark them on the map, because we have a lot of cross-roads.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Rajcic. In addition to the cross-roads that you've indicated, and I understand that this is not something that you can testify to with 100 percent accuracy, nevertheless, were there any other targets in Gracac that you believed were of sufficient military value to have targeted for artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town of Gracac, there were no such military targets, as to could have been taken into consideration for firing with a view to possibly gaining military advantage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would move for admission of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same objection, I take it Mr. -- The objection is overruled. Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P2329.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2329, map of Gracac marked by the witness, is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could now please have 65 ter 7055.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you recognise this as the first reconstruction that you put together in connection with your work for the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to take you through just a few sections of this analysis, or this reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let's move first to page 3, section 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And this is the second tab of your binder, Mr. Rajcic. Page 3, section 1 in English, and it is the same in the B/C/S. Now, in this section, Mr. Rajcic, you list the artillery which was available to the Split Military District before Kozjak 95, and specifically, you referred to the brigade artillery at section 1.2. And there you list the 4th Guards Brigade. There's an entry for the SVLR, the self-propelled multiple rocket launcher. And it indicates that it is a 128-millimetre MB 21. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 122 is what it should read.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move to page 5, section 2, and that is also the same in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And here you discuss the organisation of the artillery, specifically in section 2.1.1. You indicate that the corps artillery, that is, the artillery and artillery rocket groups, TRS-1, TRS-2, TS-3, TS-4, and TS-5 "were under the direct command of the commander of the Military District, Croatian forces." Can you tell the Trial Chamber to whom you were referring in that quoted portion.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all the elements of the artillery rocket groups and artillery groups, without the element that was detached for General Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And those artillery groups and artillery rocket groups were under the command of General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 1, 2, 3, 4, minus 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, at section 3.1 which is just towards the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could move to the next page in the English there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, you read TS-5 earlier, where the document reads TRS-five. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. That was, actually, my next question coming up, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: In section 3.1, you discuss the structure and combat deployment of the corps artillery, and I was going to ask to you look specifically at TRS-5 which appears, I believe, it is on page 7. If we go to the next page in the English version also over on the B/C/S, it lists TRS-5. However, you indicated a bit further down that several pieces of the artillery of TRS-5 were detached and sent to MUP special forces including the 122-millimetre self-propelled rocket launcher. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me a moment, please. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Would then the decision of TRS change to TS, since the rocket system was removed from that group?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at the beginning of section 4 - and this is on page 7 in the English, and page 6 in the B/C/S - you discuss -- actually, I'd like to move to 4.2.1, which is the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we move just a bit further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, in section 4.2.1 you list what you refer to as "operational level targets." For the corps artillery, that is, TS-3, TS-4, and TS-5 in the populated areas of Knin, Benkovac, and Gracac. I would like it take you through now the targets in Knin and ask you to identify those. And if you would, please, I'm going to pull up an aerial photograph of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P62.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I'm going to be making reference, Mr. Rajcic, to your reconstruction here in front of you, so if could you have that ready, we'll take these targets one by one. Now, Mr. Rajcic, given the size of this picture, what I'm going to have you do is, we're going to enlarge sections of the town to a sufficient size to allow to you identify particular targets, and then we'll proceed in that fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could please focus on the area between the listings parliament and railroad station and bring up a very large section of that. If it is possible to enlarge it a bit more. Just a little bit more. And move it a little bit to the left. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, the first target that you list in your reconstruction is of the Main Staff of the so-called VRSK in Knin. I'd like to you please circle that target on this map and place a number 1 next to it. And if you need the map to be larger, just let us know, and we can enlarge it further.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please. The -- if it can be enlarged so that it shows all the relevant parts for you, but I'd like to have it bigger, and it would be much better to have the image in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I do agree with you there, Mr. Rajcic. Unfortunately, we don't have a coloured version, but we can certainly make this bigger for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could have it enlarged a few levels more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will make it that much more difficult for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand, and when you indicate the targets, if there's a particular problem in the location of a particular target, certainly let me know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: But, Mr. Registrar, if it is possible to go a little bit larger and then move a little bit over to the right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, on this, can you please mark -- circle the location of the Main Staff of the so-called VRSK in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can recognise the location. I had a desk there for a while myself. Complete with the former JNA hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I mark with 1 or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the next target that you list is the headquarters of the Ministry of Defence of the so-called RSK in Knin. Can you please circle that target on this map and place a number 2 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to have the coordinates here. But I do believe that it was the same building. I found that in the office where I had my desk as the chief of artillery, there used to be the office of an official of the Ministry of Defence of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, can you also place a 2 underneath -- or right next to where you had the 1.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And the third target you list is the communication centre of the so-called VRSK in Knin, and I'd like to you please circle that target and place a number 3 next to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, just for the record the two adjacent rectangles were marked in the beginning, so to cover 1, and then 2 to be included, and the two not separate. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, if could you please circle the communication centre which you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the communication centre, I think it was housed in the main post office, which housed the communication system of the entire general area. I will try to pinpoint the exact location as far as I can, though a margin of error is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you thank you very much for that. And the fourth target you list is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness added a 3 to that marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The fourth target that you list is barracks in the area of the town of Knin. And I wasn't certain from reading that whether you were referring to one barracks or more than one barracks. Perhaps you could tell us that first, and then we can decide moving this photograph or not.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- should I -- it says here "barracks" in plural. Barracks in the general area of Knin and in other towns, there were the total of 17 military installations from Grahovo through to Velebit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Before we move on let me simply move this into evidence. I'll offer this at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2330.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2330 is admitted into evidence. English is not my mother tongue, Mr. Russo. But I do understand that barracks, although linguistically, is plural, nevertheless could refer to one single construction even. So, therefore, the plural and the singular, we should be very careful to ask about more barracks or one barracks because one barracks is still the plural.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's what I'm attempting to discover, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: In terms of the target that you indicated here in your reconstruction, which barracks in Knin are you referring to? And if you're referring to more than one, tell us which ones.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first and most important is the Slavko Rodic barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could please Exhibit P62 brought up again, we'll have that area enlarged for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we move it all the way over to the left, I believe it will ... and a bit up. Actually, if we could zoom out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, if you could simply circle the area of the barracks, the Slavko Rodic barracks, and mark it with the number 4.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before we move on -- well, we will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we can have this marked and admitted, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2331, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2331 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Russo, if you would have asked the witness whether the portion marked and mentioned and referred to as Knin army barracks would, be the barracks he meant, we would have been far more efficient. Saves an exhibit. Northern barracks is -- that's apparently the only issue. Let's not waste more time on it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could have again P62 brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And the next target you list, Mr. Rajcic, is the railway station in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move the photograph over to the right and a bit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If could you please circle that target and place the number 5 next to it. Oh, my apologies. I believe the next target you in fact listed was the police station in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move the photograph over to the left. A bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now if you could identify for us the location of that target and place a 5 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent I can find my way here, this is where the police station was. I'll put a 5 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could have this now marked and admitted. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I did this with the reservation that I need the X and Y coordinates to mark this. But we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. That's understood, Mr. Rajcic. Thank you. Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You tender it into evidence. No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P2332, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.
